purpose: Personal-investment research only. Robotics claims are checked against issuer disclosures and current market evidence before affecting the framework.

framework.summary: Adoption is ranked by task structure and customer payback, not by how human-like the machine looks. August 21-22 evidence strengthens, rather than changes, the sequence.

waves.name: Structured logistics + fixed industrial automation
waves.why: Controlled environments, repeatable tasks, mature safety practices and measurable labour and throughput ROI.

waves.name: Cobots + mobile manipulation + constrained service robots
waves.why: AI expands task coverage while deployments remain geofenced, supervised and workflow-specific.

waves.name: Industrial humanoids
waves.why: Human-shaped facilities help, but dexterity, reliability, battery life, safety, training-data depth and total cost still need proof.

waves.name: Open-world consumer robots
waves.why: Unstructured environments compound edge cases, liability and price sensitivity.

currentRead.commercialSignal: Warehouse/fixed automation remains the strongest public-market evidence set. Rockwell Automation's fiscal Q3 2026 organic sales rose 10% and guidance increased; Symbotic, Geekplus and Cognex remain cleaner direct enabling-layer exposures. Geekplus also launched RoboShuttle Hyper on August 12, reinforcing continued product iteration in structured fulfilment rather than a shift toward general-purpose humanoids.
currentRead.humanoidSignal: China's humanoid ecosystem is scaling fast, but the newest public evidence still argues against moving humanoids ahead of fixed automation. Unitree's CEO says the embodied-intelligence breakthrough could still be two to ten years away and explicitly acknowledged weak real-world application. ACE Robotics expects a software breakthrough by late 2027 but says broad commercial implementation could take another four to five years; it identifies training-data scarcity as a major bottleneck. AiMOGA has delivered more than 3,000 robots, including 2,000 overseas, but economics and repeat-use productivity remain insufficiently disclosed for Power Stack promotion.
currentRead.chinaScaleSignal: Industry data cited by Reuters says China delivered more than 40,000 humanoids in the first half of 2026 and accounts for roughly 97% of global shipments. This is strategically important manufacturing scale, but shipment volume does not yet equal attractive customer ROI or OEM margins.
currentRead.portfolioImplication: Keep fixed automation, machine vision, motion/control and cobot exposure ahead of humanoid OEMs until paid deployments, repeat orders, utilisation and unit economics are consistently visible. High post-IPO valuations increase the penalty for confusing technology progress with investable economics.

priorityCandidate.name: Rockwell Automation
priorityCandidate.thesis: Profitable broad industrial-automation exposure across controls, drives, motion, software and factory systems; directly positioned in the first commercial automation wave rather than dependent on humanoid optionality.
priorityCandidate.evidence: Fiscal Q3 2026 sales rose 8%, organic sales rose 10%, enterprise operating margin reached 22.3%, free cash flow was $654m, and FY2026 organic-sales guidance was raised to 7.5%-9.5% with adjusted EPS guidance of $13.00-$13.30.

screenedOutOrDeferred.name: Unitree
screenedOutOrDeferred.reason: Commercial credibility and profitability improve sector validation, but the roughly $50bn post-debut valuation and still-limited commercial deployment fail the entry-quality bar.

screenedOutOrDeferred.name: Chery Automobile
screenedOutOrDeferred.reason: AiMOGA robotics optionality is real and deployments are growing, but robotics is still diluted inside the auto group and stand-alone economics are not disclosed well enough to justify promotion.
Commercial deployment is real, but current revenue scale and cash-burn economics do not clear the Power Stack bar.
Robotics exposure remains diluted within SoftBank's conglomerate and investment-portfolio risk.

notes: Training data and world-model reliability are now explicit humanoid bottlenecks alongside hardware cost and safety.
China's shipment leadership strengthens the component/supply-chain research case more than it justifies chasing newly listed humanoid OEMs.
